scr_ap_using_the_accounts_payable_applic.purpose: Frames the A/P book as a whole: which functions live on the Accounts Payable menu versus the Setup tab, so an accountant taking over an owner's portfolio knows where invoice entry, payment runs, subledger close and 1099 processing each sit before touching a live property.
scr_ap_using_the_accounts_payable_applic.outcome: The accountant can locate any A/P function by menu section instead of guessing, and knows that configuration changes live behind a separate guide and a separate permission set.
scr_ap_using_the_accounts_payable_applic.rootCause: Offshore teams are dropped onto an owner's RealPage instance mid-cycle with no orientation, and the expensive mistakes are navigational — entering a manual payment when a check run was intended, or changing a setup default while trying to fix one invoice. Separating daily tasks from configuration up front is what prevents a one-invoice problem becoming a portfolio-wide one.
scr_ap_using_the_accounts_payable_applic.ifSkipped: New staff learn the menu by trial and error on live properties, and setup defaults get changed while chasing a single coding error.
redFlags: Daily-task staff holding Setup-tab permissions
Configuration changed to work around a single mis-coded invoice
New portfolio onboarded without a documented menu-to-task map
scr_ap_using_the_accounts_payable_applic.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the Payables menu (Payable Entry, Check Processing, Vendor, 1099 Processing) with Setup > Payables configuration behind separate menu security.

scr_ap_accounts_payable.purpose: The Accounts Payable application root — the entry point that carries the A/P home page, the menu and the subscription/permission boundary that decides which A/P features a given user's role can even see for the properties assigned to them.
scr_ap_accounts_payable.outcome: The user lands in A/P scoped to the properties and functions their role permits, with the home page showing what is pending for them.
scr_ap_accounts_payable.rootCause: In a multi-owner management company one RealPage instance serves many ownership entities, and A/P is the module with the most direct path to cash out the door. Access has to be property-scoped at the application boundary, because an accountant who can see every property's payment selection can create a disbursement for an entity they do not serve.
scr_ap_accounts_payable.ifSkipped: Users see and act on properties outside their assignment, and the property-level access review auditors request cannot be evidenced.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 10 — control activities and segregation of duties
SOC 1 Type II — logical access controls at the service organization
redFlags: A/P roles granted across all properties rather than an assigned list
Terminated staff still holding A/P application access
One login shared across an offshore shift
scr_ap_accounts_payable.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the Payables module reached through the role menu, with property-list security from Administration > Security controlling which entities appear.

scr_ap_overview_of_the_accounts_payable_.purpose: Explains what A/P actually does end to end — vendor accounts, invoice entry and edit, an optional multi-level approval cycle, quick check entry, dual signature thresholds, and applying vendor overpayments to the next invoice — plus the rule that paid invoices can no longer be deleted or materially edited.
scr_ap_overview_of_the_accounts_payable_.outcome: The accountant understands the full payable lifecycle and, critically, which point in it is the last chance to correct an invoice before it locks.
scr_ap_overview_of_the_accounts_payable_.rootCause: The single most-repeated A/P error is discovering wrong property or GL coding after the check cleared, when the record is locked and the only remedy is a reclassifying journal entry that an owner will ask about. Knowing the lock point up front changes where the accountant puts their review effort — into coding before approval, not into corrections afterwards.
scr_ap_overview_of_the_accounts_payable_.ifSkipped: Coding is reviewed after payment rather than before it, and the month fills with reclass journal entries that owners question in the variance call.
gaap: ASC 405-10 — recognition and derecognition of liabilities
redFlags: Reclass volume rising month over month, signalling coding review happens too late
Quick check entry used to bypass the approval cycle
Dual-signature threshold set above the typical capital invoice size
scr_ap_overview_of_the_accounts_payable_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the Payables lifecycle (Payable Entry > PAYscan workflow approval > Check Processing), where a posted and paid payable must be voided rather than edited.

scr_ap_accounts_payable_menu.purpose: The All-tab menu listing every A/P destination — Approval workbench, Vendors, A/P invoices, Invoice research, Payments, check runs, open/close subledger, print payment copies, print FAS and the check register — which is the working map an accountant uses to run a day in A/P.
scr_ap_accounts_payable_menu.outcome: Each task in the daily A/P cycle maps to a known menu option, including the less obvious ones like Invoice research and Print FAS.
scr_ap_accounts_payable_menu.rootCause: Two menu options here look interchangeable and are not: the A/P invoices list preloads records, while Invoice research deliberately does not, which is the only workable search on a portfolio with hundreds of thousands of historic invoices. Staff who do not know the difference time out the invoice list during an owner query instead of using research.
scr_ap_accounts_payable_menu.ifSkipped: Accountants run the wrong list for the job, sessions time out on large portfolios, and subledger open/close options are missed at month end.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 12 — deployment through policies and procedures
redFlags: Menu options hidden by permission that the accountant's SOP still requires
Close Subledger not used, leaving prior periods open to backdated invoices
Staff using the preloading invoice list for portfolio-wide searches
scr_ap_accounts_payable_menu.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the Payables side menu with Payable > Find for research-style lookups and Financials > Closing > Post Month for the subledger open/close equivalent.

scr_ap_approval_workbench.purpose: The single queue where A/P invoices, payment requests and expense reports awaiting authorization are approved or declined, applying the approval matrix that ties each approver to a property list and a dollar ceiling.
scr_ap_approval_workbench.outcome: Transactions move forward only with an authorization record showing who approved what, at which level, and when.
scr_ap_approval_workbench.rootCause: Delegated authority in a management agreement is meaningless unless a system enforces it at the moment of approval. The workbench is where segregation of duties becomes real — the person who keyed the invoice must not be the person who clears it — and it is the artifact auditors sample when testing SOX 404 authorization controls.
scr_ap_approval_workbench.ifSkipped: Invoices are paid on verbal authority, self-approval goes undetected, and the owner's delegation-of-authority limits exist only on paper.
redFlags: Same user id as preparer and approver on an invoice
Approvals granted above the approver's dollar limit
Invoices sitting in the queue past vendor terms, creating late fees
Bulk approval of an entire queue in a single action
scr_ap_approval_workbench.yardi: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan / Procure to Pay workflow approvals with the 'My Approvals' inbox and approval routing by property and amount.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers.purpose: The vendor master chapter — adding and maintaining supplier records carrying remit-to address, TIN and 1099 designation, terms, insurance certificates and banking details, the data set that drives every payment and every year-end information return.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers.outcome: Payments go to a verified payee at a verified address or bank account, and year-end reporting can be produced from the master without reconstruction.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers.rootCause: Vendor master is the highest-value target in property accounting fraud: a single unverified remit-to or bank change redirects an entire month of contractor payments. It is also the only place W-9 and TIN data lives, so a gap there becomes an IRS penalty in January rather than an inconvenience in June.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers.ifSkipped: Payments reach fraudulent bank accounts, 1099s are filed with missing or mismatched TINs, and uninsured contractors work on the property.
gaap: IRC §6109 and §3406 — TIN and backup withholding
redFlags: Bank detail changed without an independent call-back to a known number
Vendor address matching an employee address
Active vendors with expired general liability or workers' compensation certificates
Duplicate vendor records for the same TIN
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor (remit-to, 1099, terms, insurance) with VendorCafe for vendor self-service onboarding and compliance documents.

scr_ap_a_p_invoices.purpose: The invoice chapter covering how vendor bills are entered, coded to property and GL account, held, released and ultimately paid — the mechanism by which an obligation becomes a 2010 Accounts Payable balance and an expense line on the owner's operating statement.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices.outcome: Each vendor bill lands on the right property, the right account and the right accounting period, and is visible on the aging until it is settled.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices.rootCause: Every number an owner sees in NOI starts as an invoice coded by someone at a keyboard. Two decisions made at that moment — which property bears the cost and whether it is a repair or an improvement — set the operating statement, the budget variance commentary and the depreciable basis, and neither is cheap to reverse once the period closes.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices.ifSkipped: Costs land on the wrong property or the wrong period, capital work is expensed, and NOI reported to the lender and the owner is wrong.
gaap: ASC 360-10 and Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — capital versus repair
redFlags: Repeat invoice numbers for the same vendor
Service period spanning the period end with no accrual split
Turn and make-ready costs coded to capital to protect a repairs budget
Invoices entered with a posting date later than the service date to dodge a closed period
scr_ap_a_p_invoices.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable Entry or Payable Batch, with OCR-captured invoices routed through PAYscan > Invoice Register.

scr_ap_payments.purpose: The payment chapter describing how approved invoices become disbursements — the selection run, the funding check against property available cash, the method chosen, and the answers to the questions that recur every check cycle about timing and reversals.
scr_ap_payments.outcome: Approved, due invoices are paid from the correct property bank account by the correct method, and the disbursement is recorded against the specific invoices it settles.
scr_ap_payments.rootCause: Property-level cash is not fungible across an owner's portfolio. Each entity has its own operating account, its own lender-controlled balances and its own owner funding rhythm, so the payment run has to respect both vendor terms and what is actually in that property's 1110 Operating Cash on the day, or the accountant creates an overdraft in one entity while another sits on idle cash.
scr_ap_payments.ifSkipped: Payments overdraw a property account or get funded from the wrong entity, creating unintended due to/due from balances and bank fees.
gaap: UCC Article 3 and §4-404 — negotiable instruments and stale checks
31 CFR Part 501 — OFAC screening of payees
redFlags: Payment run exceeding the property's available cash
One property's bank account funding another entity's vendors
Payments released without the approval queue cleared
Positive pay file not transmitted the same day checks print
scr_ap_payments.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Processing (Create Checks / Auto Pay filtered by bank and property) and Payables > EFT for ACH files.

scr_ap_daily_tasks.purpose: The daily A/P operating rhythm — the recurring work of entering and coding the day's invoices, clearing the held queue, answering vendor calls and keeping the aging current so nothing accumulates into a month-end surprise.
scr_ap_daily_tasks.outcome: Invoices are captured the day they arrive, the held queue is worked down, and the aging reflects reality rather than a backlog in someone's inbox.
scr_ap_daily_tasks.rootCause: A/P backlog is silent until close. Invoices that sit uncoded for three weeks are the ones that become unrecorded liabilities at period end, and the offshore shift model makes that worse because a question asked at 9pm US time waits a full cycle for an answer. Daily cadence is the control that keeps the accrual complete.
scr_ap_daily_tasks.ifSkipped: Invoices pile up unrecorded, month-end accruals are guesses, and vendors move the property to cash-on-delivery terms.
redFlags: Invoice batches dated days after receipt
A held queue that never drops below a constant level
Utility bills entered only when the shut-off notice arrives
scr_ap_daily_tasks.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the daily Payables cycle — Payable Entry, PAYscan exception queue and the Payables > Find aged unposted list.

scr_ap_enter_ap_invoices_section.purpose: Introduces the Daily tasks section of the A/P menu and what each option within it does, positioning invoice entry as the front of the section rather than an isolated screen.
scr_ap_enter_ap_invoices_section.outcome: The accountant knows which daily-task option to reach for — direct entry, batch entry, quick entry or the held queue — before opening any of them.
scr_ap_enter_ap_invoices_section.rootCause: RealPage offers several routes to the same posted payable, and they carry different control profiles: quick entry trades approval routing for speed, batch entry gives a reviewable total, single entry gives full coding detail. Choosing without knowing the trade-off is how an invoice ends up posted without ever passing an approver.
scr_ap_enter_ap_invoices_section.ifSkipped: Staff default to whichever entry route they learned first, and high-value invoices enter through the path with the weakest approval routing.
redFlags: Quick entry used for invoices above the approval threshold
Batch totals not agreed to the physical invoice stack before posting
Entry method chosen by habit rather than by invoice value
scr_ap_enter_ap_invoices_section.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the Payables entry choices — Payable Entry, Payable Batch and quick-entry style batch screens, each with different workflow routing.

scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices_2.purpose: Describes the pay-invoices workflow including applying credits such as advances and adjustments, choosing between immediate processing and approve-then-pay, parking payment requests in the Outbox, and starting payment from either the invoice page or the invoice list.
scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices_2.outcome: Invoices are settled net of available credits and advances, through the method their vendor is set up for, with the payment request traceable back to its originating invoices.
scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices_2.rootCause: Credits and advances sitting unapplied on a vendor account are money the owner already paid. A contractor deposit for a roof job or a utility credit from a billing correction only reduces cash if the payment workflow picks it up at selection time; once the full invoice is paid, recovering it means chasing the vendor for a refund check.
scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices_2.ifSkipped: Vendors are paid gross while their credit balances age, and contractor advances get expensed twice when the final invoice posts.
redFlags: Debit-balance vendors still being paid in full
Payment requests left in the Outbox past the invoice due date
Advances not relieved when the final invoice is paid
scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices_2.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Processing where open credits on the vendor net against selected payables in the same check run.

scr_ap_a_p_adjustments.purpose: Covers A/P adjustments — vendor credit memos, debit memos and corrections that change what is owed without a cash movement, typically surfaced during the month-end vendor statement reconciliation.
scr_ap_a_p_adjustments.outcome: The vendor's balance in the subledger agrees to the vendor's own statement, with each difference explained by a recorded adjustment.
scr_ap_a_p_adjustments.rootCause: Vendor statement reconciliation is where duplicate payments and missing credits are actually found. A landscaping vendor that credited a missed service in March shows a lower balance on their statement than the aging does, and unless that credit is recorded the difference just sits there until an auditor asks — or until the property pays for a service it already got credited for.
scr_ap_a_p_adjustments.ifSkipped: The A/P aging drifts away from vendor statements, credits expire unused, and duplicate payments stay hidden inside the variance.
gaap: ASC 450 — recognition when a disputed amount is resolved
redFlags: Debit memos raised with no vendor correspondence behind them
Credits recorded but never applied to an invoice
Adjustments posted to a suspense account instead of the original expense line
scr_ap_a_p_adjustments.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable Entry with a negative amount for credit memos, applied during check processing.

scr_ap_a_p_advances.purpose: Covers advance payments — contractor mobilization deposits, prepaid service retainers and similar amounts paid before the work is performed — and how they are tracked so the advance is relieved against the final invoice rather than expensed twice.
scr_ap_a_p_advances.outcome: The advance sits as an asset until the vendor delivers, then offsets the final invoice, leaving one expense charge for one piece of work.
scr_ap_a_p_advances.rootCause: Capital and turn contractors routinely demand deposits before mobilizing. If that cheque is coded straight to 6110 Repairs & Maintenance, the expense hits in the payment month, hits again when the completion invoice posts, and the owner's budget variance for both months is wrong in opposite directions with nothing on the balance sheet to explain it.
scr_ap_a_p_advances.ifSkipped: Deposits are expensed on payment and again on completion, doubling cost in the period and leaving the advance unrecoverable if the vendor walks.
redFlags: Advances outstanding beyond the contract completion date
Deposits coded directly to expense rather than 1310 Prepaid Expenses
Advance not applied when the final invoice was paid
scr_ap_a_p_advances.yardi: Yardi Voyager: prepayment payables coded to a prepaid GL account and applied against the vendor's final payable at check processing.

scr_ap_payment_methods.purpose: Surveys the available disbursement methods — printed check, online check delivery, cash, credit card, electronic funds transfer and manual payment — with how each is set up and how invoices are paid through it.
scr_ap_payment_methods.outcome: Each vendor is paid by the method their record specifies, with the control appropriate to that method applied before funds move.
scr_ap_payment_methods.rootCause: The methods carry sharply different risk. A printed check runs through numbered negotiable stock and a positive pay file; an ACH leaves the same day under NACHA rules with no recall window; a card payment lands in 2140 Credit Card Payable and reconciles on a statement cycle, not a bank cycle. Treating them as interchangeable is how an urgent wire skips every control the check run would have applied.
scr_ap_payment_methods.ifSkipped: Vendors are paid by whichever method is fastest that day, and the controls attached to the intended method never run.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — ACH entries and prenotes
UCC Article 3 — checks as negotiable instruments
redFlags: Vendors flipped to ACH without a prenote or independent bank verification
Card payments never reconciled to 2140 Credit Card Payable
Wires used routinely for spend that belongs in the check run
scr_ap_payment_methods.yardi: Yardi Voyager: check printing from Check Processing, ACH via Payables > EFT, and manual check entry for wires and handwritten cheques.

scr_ap_banking.purpose: The Banking section of the A/P menu — where property bank accounts, check stock and numbering, positive pay and electronic payment origination settings connect A/P disbursements to the cash accounts they draw on.
scr_ap_banking.outcome: Each property's payments originate from its own designated bank account with the correct check sequence and bank-side fraud controls in place.
scr_ap_banking.rootCause: Every operating entity in an institutional portfolio has a lender-required or owner-required bank account, and A/P is what draws on it. Bind the wrong bank to a property and the payment run debits another owner's cash — a real intercompany receivable that has to be repaid, disclosed, and explained during the annual audit of related-party balances.
scr_ap_banking.ifSkipped: Payments draw on the wrong entity's cash, unintended affiliate balances build up, and positive pay never reaches the bank for a check run.
gaap: ASC 810 — entity separateness in consolidated reporting
State security deposit trust account statutes
redFlags: A/P able to draw on the 1115 Security Deposit Trust Cash account
Property mapped to a bank account belonging to a different ownership entity
Check number sequences overlapping between properties on the same account
scr_ap_banking.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Setup > Bank (cash GL account, check layout and MICR, next check number, positive pay and ACH origination) with bank assignment on the property.

scr_ap_periodic_tasks.purpose: The Periodic Tasks section of the A/P menu — the cycle-based work that runs at period end rather than daily: subledger close, management fee calculation, recurring invoice generation and the batch summaries that support them.
scr_ap_periodic_tasks.outcome: The month-end A/P sequence runs in order, and the accountant knows which of these tasks must complete before the subledger can be closed.
scr_ap_periodic_tasks.rootCause: Periodic tasks have dependencies that daily tasks do not. Management fees cannot calculate until the revenue they are based on is final, recurring invoices must generate before the accrual review, and the subledger cannot close until both have posted. Running them out of sequence means reopening a closed period after the owner package has already gone out.
scr_ap_periodic_tasks.ifSkipped: Period-end steps run out of order or get missed, and the subledger closes on an incomplete population of payables.
gaap: ASC 405-10 — completeness at the reporting date
redFlags: Subledger closed before recurring invoices generated
Management fees calculated on a revenue figure that later changed
Periodic tasks run by whoever is available rather than a named owner per property
scr_ap_periodic_tasks.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Closing > Post Month per property, Tools > Post Recurring Payables and Financials > Management Fees.

scr_ap_periodic_tasks_overview.purpose: Lists what sits inside Periodic Tasks — Site View into the Spend Management site experience, Approval Workbench Views, Close Subledger and Open Subledger, subledger summaries, and the Fees option that calculates and posts management fees.
scr_ap_periodic_tasks_overview.outcome: The accountant can identify the specific periodic option needed for a given close step, including the subledger open/close pair that bounds the period.
scr_ap_periodic_tasks_overview.rootCause: Close Subledger and Open Subledger are the two options on this menu with the sharpest consequences. Closing is what stops a site manager entering an invoice into a month whose financials have already reached the owner; reopening is a documented exception that a reviewer should see. Bundling them with routine periodic options hides how much weight they carry.
scr_ap_periodic_tasks_overview.ifSkipped: Subledgers stay open after reporting, invoices post into reported periods, and the owner's issued statements silently stop agreeing to the system.
gaap: ASC 250 — error correction when a reported period changes
redFlags: Subledger reopened with no documented reason or approver
Site View users entering invoices into a period being closed
Approval workbench views filtered so a class of invoices is invisible to approvers
scr_ap_periodic_tasks_overview.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Closing > Post Month and Reopen Month per property, with site-staff access through property-list security.

scr_ap_a_p_subledger.purpose: Covers opening and closing A/P summaries and managing the transactions inside them — the control mechanism that fixes a period's payable population and keeps the aging agreeing to the 2010 Accounts Payable control account.
scr_ap_a_p_subledger.outcome: At each period end the A/P aging total equals the GL control balance, and the period is locked so that total cannot change after reporting.
scr_ap_a_p_subledger.rootCause: The subledger-to-control tie is the one A/P reconciliation an auditor will always test, and it only holds if closing actually prevents further posting. An open prior period on a 40-property portfolio means any one site can add an invoice to a month whose statements already went to the investor, and the accountant discovers it when next month's opening balance does not roll.
scr_ap_a_p_subledger.ifSkipped: The aging and the control account diverge, the difference has no explanation, and auditors treat it as a key control failure.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 13 — relevant information for reconciliation
redFlags: Aging total not equal to the 2010 Accounts Payable balance at period end
Prior periods still open after the owner package shipped
Reconciling items carried forward month after month with the same description
scr_ap_a_p_subledger.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Closing > Post Month locks Payables per property, with the Aged Payables report tied to the GL control account.

scr_ap_fees.purpose: Covers setting up fees, generating the A/P and A/R invoices that record them, and tracking and recalculating management fees — the affiliate charge that flows from the property entity to the management company each month.
scr_ap_fees.outcome: Management fees are calculated on the base the management agreement defines, recorded on both sides of the affiliate relationship, and recalculable when the revenue base changes.
scr_ap_fees.rootCause: The management fee is simultaneously an expense of the property, revenue of the manager and a related-party transaction requiring disclosure. Because it is usually 2 to 4 percent of effective gross income, any late revenue adjustment moves the fee, and a fee that was not recalculated after a concession true-up is both a GAAP measurement error and a contractual overcharge the owner can demand back.
scr_ap_fees.ifSkipped: Fees are billed on a stale revenue base, the affiliate balances do not eliminate, and the owner's fee audit produces a refund claim.
gaap: IRC §482 — arm's-length pricing between related parties
redFlags: Fee base including items the management agreement excludes, such as utility reimbursement or other income
Fee not recalculated after a revenue adjustment posted
Affiliate fee payable and receivable not agreeing between entities
scr_ap_fees.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Management Fees with the fee basis defined per property, calculating and posting a payable to the management company.

scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices.purpose: Covers creating and maintaining recurring A/P invoices — the fixed monthly obligations such as landscaping contracts, pest control, elevator maintenance, alarm monitoring and equipment leases that generate on a schedule rather than from an arriving bill.
scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices.outcome: Fixed contract costs post every month without waiting for a paper invoice, and each schedule carries a start and end date matching its contract.
scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices.rootCause: Recurring schedules are a completeness control with an expiry problem. They ensure the elevator contract never gets missed at accrual time, but an operating-expense schedule that outlives its terminated contract keeps paying a vendor who no longer serves the property, and nobody notices because the amount is identical every month and never appears as a variance.
scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices.ifSkipped: Fixed monthly costs are missed from the accrual, or schedules for cancelled contracts keep generating payments nobody reviews.
gaap: ASC 842 — recurring equipment lease payments where the contract is a lease
redFlags: Recurring schedules with no end date
Amount unchanged across a contract renewal that raised the rate
Schedules still active for a property that has been sold
Equipment lease schedules not assessed under ASC 842
scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Recurring Payable with frequency and start/end period, posted via Tools > Post Recurring Payables.

scr_ap_account_maintenance.purpose: Covers routine maintenance of the GL accounts A/P codes to — adding accounts for a new property or owner reporting line, correcting account attributes, and retiring accounts that should no longer receive postings.
scr_ap_account_maintenance.outcome: The account list A/P staff pick from matches the owner's current reporting format, with obsolete accounts inactivated rather than deleted.
scr_ap_account_maintenance.rootCause: Each institutional owner maps the operating chart to their own reporting template, and A/P coding is where that mapping either holds or breaks. Deleting an account that carries history orphans prior-year invoices and breaks the comparative column in the owner package; inactivating it preserves the history while keeping it off the coding list.
scr_ap_account_maintenance.ifSkipped: Accountants code to accounts that no longer map to an owner reporting line, and deleted accounts break prior-period comparatives.
gaap: ASC 205 and ASC 220 — financial statement presentation
HUD Handbook 4370.2 — prescribed chart for HUD-insured properties
redFlags: Accounts with posting history deleted rather than inactivated
New accounts created without a mapping to the owner's reporting line
Duplicate accounts for the same expense type created by different regions
scr_ap_account_maintenance.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Setup > Chart of Accounts > Account (add, edit, inactivate) and Financials > Account Trees for reporting groupings.

scr_ap_expense_reports.purpose: Covers creating, submitting and approving expense reports so employees, properties and P-card holders are reimbursed — the route by which mileage, travel, supplies bought at retail and card spend enter A/P without a vendor invoice.
scr_ap_expense_reports.outcome: Reimbursable spend is substantiated, approved, coded to the property that benefited, and settled through 2150 Employee Reimbursements Payable.
scr_ap_expense_reports.rootCause: Expense reports are the only A/P stream where the payee is also the preparer and the substantiation is a photographed receipt. Under an accountable plan the business purpose and receipt must exist or the reimbursement becomes taxable W-2 wages — and in property operations these items routinely carry someone else's cost, such as a maintenance tech buying parts for a sister property on a card assigned to this one.
scr_ap_expense_reports.ifSkipped: Reimbursements are paid without substantiation, become taxable wages on audit, and property-level costs land on whichever property issued the card.
gaap: IRC §274(d) — substantiation of travel and related expense
redFlags: Expense reports approved by the submitter's direct report
Items of $75 or more with no receipt attached
Card spend coded to whichever property issued the card rather than the one that benefited
Reimbursements paid before approval completed
scr_ap_expense_reports.yardi: Yardi Voyager: no native expense-report module — reimbursements are entered as payables to an employee vendor, or handled through Procure to Pay expense workflow.

scr_ap_assets.purpose: Covers adding and maintaining asset records created out of A/P activity — appliances, HVAC units, flooring packages and FF&E purchased through vendor invoices that exceed the owner's capitalization threshold.
scr_ap_assets.outcome: Capital purchases entering through A/P become tracked asset records with category, location and in-service date, ready for depreciation.
scr_ap_assets.rootCause: The capitalization decision happens at invoice coding, but the asset record is what makes it durable. Without one, a $6,000 rooftop HVAC unit sits as a number in 1540 FF&E with no identity, so when it is replaced four years later nobody retires the original and 1590 Accumulated Depreciation keeps running against equipment that left the property in a dumpster.
scr_ap_assets.ifSkipped: Capitalized purchases have no asset identity, disposals are never recorded, and the fixed asset register stops agreeing to the balance sheet.
gaap: Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-1(f) — de minimis safe harbor
redFlags: Capital invoices posted with no asset record created
Invoices split below the capitalization threshold to avoid capitalizing
Replaced equipment still depreciating alongside its replacement
In-service date set to the invoice date rather than the date placed in service
scr_ap_assets.yardi: Yardi Voyager Fixed Assets: Fixed Assets > Asset created from the payable, with class, method and life driving Fixed Assets > Depreciation.

scr_ap_bids_and_contracts.purpose: Covers the Contracts option on the A/P menu, available through the Unified Platform when the Bids and Contracts product is integrated — vendor bids, awarded contracts and the change orders that govern what a contractor may bill on a renovation or capital project.
scr_ap_bids_and_contracts.outcome: Contractor spend is bounded by an approved contract value, and invoices above it require a documented change order before they can be paid.
scr_ap_bids_and_contracts.rootCause: Value-add renovation programs are where property portfolios lose the most money quietly. A contract with a schedule of values and retainage gives the accountant something to match invoices against; without it, progress billings are approved on the strength of the property manager's recollection, and the overrun only becomes visible when the capex budget is already blown.
scr_ap_bids_and_contracts.ifSkipped: Contractors bill above the awarded amount without a change order, retainage is not withheld, and lender draw packages cannot be supported.
gaap: State mechanic's lien and lien waiver statutes

Retainage not withheld on progress billings
Conditional lien waivers missing for the billed period
Final payment released before the lien waiver period expired
scr_ap_bids_and_contracts.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Service Contracts and Job Cost > Contract with change orders; bid management through Yardi Construction Manager.

scr_ap_full_service.purpose: Describes Full Service Spend Management, which integrates RealPage Invoice Processing with RealPage Accounting so scanned vendor invoices create A/P invoices without manual keying, subject to subscription.
scr_ap_full_service.outcome: Invoices arrive in A/P already captured and coded by the outsourced processor, with the property team handling only exceptions.
scr_ap_full_service.rootCause: Outsourcing the keystrokes does not outsource the control. The owner still carries responsibility for coding accuracy and approval, which means the complementary user-entity controls named in the provider's SOC 1 report — exception review and invoice approval — have to actually be performed, not assumed to be part of the service.
scr_ap_full_service.ifSkipped: The outsourced stream is treated as pre-validated, exception queues go unreviewed, and auditors cannot rely on the process at all.
gaap: AICPA SSAE 18 and AU-C 402 — service organization controls
COSO 2013 Principle 16 — ongoing evaluation of outsourced providers
redFlags: SOC 1 Type II report never obtained or never read
Exception queue with items older than the vendor payment terms
Auto-coded invoices approved without a human review of the GL account
scr_ap_full_service.yardi: Yardi Voyager: no direct equivalent; the closest is outsourced invoice capture through PAYscan and Yardi Invoice Processing Services.

scr_ap_scanning.purpose: Describes the single-scan feature that uses a desktop scanner to capture a document and attach it directly to an A/P invoice, purchase order or service contract without an intermediate file-and-upload step.
scr_ap_scanning.outcome: The source document is attached to the transaction it supports at the moment of entry, and travels with it into approval and audit.
scr_ap_scanning.rootCause: An invoice without its image is unapprovable and, at year end, undefendable. Approvers reviewing remotely cannot judge a coding decision from an amount alone, and when the IRS or the auditor samples a repairs charge two years later the deduction stands or falls on whether the scanned invoice is retrievable from the record.
scr_ap_scanning.ifSkipped: Approvers sign off blind on amounts alone, and sampled transactions have no retrievable support at audit.
gaap: IRC §6001 and Treas. Reg. §1.6001-1 — records retention
COSO 2013 — supporting documentation for control activities
redFlags: Invoices approved with no image attached
Scans that are illegible, cropped or are a vendor statement rather than the invoice
Documents attached to the wrong invoice number
scr_ap_scanning.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Document Management attachments on the payable, and PAYscan invoice image capture linked to the invoice register.

scr_ap_help_and_support.purpose: Points to the support tools available in the RealPage Financial Suite — documentation, knowledge base and case submission — the route an accountant uses when the system blocks a posting rather than when the accounting is in question.
scr_ap_help_and_support.outcome: System-level blockers reach RealPage support with an error id and reproduction steps instead of being worked around locally.
scr_ap_help_and_support.rootCause: At month end the difference between a two-hour and a two-day close is how fast a blocker such as a locked period, a failed check run or a subledger that will not close gets escalated. An offshore team working a US close overnight has one shift to raise it; a workaround invented at 3am is what turns a system issue into an accounting error nobody can explain later.
scr_ap_help_and_support.ifSkipped: Staff invent undocumented workarounds during close, and the resulting entries cannot be defended to a reviewer or an auditor.
redFlags: Recurring close blockers never raised as a support case
Workarounds applied during close with no written record
Support cases opened without the error id or screenshot, delaying resolution
scr_ap_help_and_support.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Yardi Client Central for support cases and knowledge base, with Yardi Aspire for training.

scr_ap_appendices.purpose: The reference section at the back of the A/P book holding supplementary material — field references, code lists and detail an accountant consults occasionally rather than working through in sequence.
scr_ap_appendices.outcome: Detailed reference material is findable when a specific field or code meaning is in question during entry or review.
scr_ap_appendices.rootCause: Reference detail is what an accountant reaches for under pressure — decoding a status value on an aged invoice, or confirming what a particular field controls before changing it on a live record. Material buried at the back of a guide that nobody knows exists gets replaced by guesswork on exactly the transactions that are unusual enough to matter.
scr_ap_appendices.ifSkipped: Unusual records are interpreted from their labels alone, and status or code meanings are guessed during owner queries and audit sampling.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 13 — quality information for control operation
redFlags: Status codes interpreted by guesswork during an owner query
Reference material not included in offshore onboarding packs
scr_ap_appendices.yardi: Yardi Voyager: equivalent reference detail lives in Client Central documentation and the field-level help on Payables screens.

scr_ap_configuring_accounts_payable.purpose: The configuration book covering the Setup tab of the A/P menu — the settings that decide how invoices are numbered, how approvals route, which payment methods exist and what the daily-task users are allowed to do.
scr_ap_configuring_accounts_payable.outcome: A/P behaves consistently across every entity in the portfolio, with configuration changes made deliberately rather than as a side effect of fixing a transaction.
scr_ap_configuring_accounts_payable.rootCause: Configuration is portfolio-wide while transactions are property-specific, and staff frequently confuse the two. Loosening a duplicate-invoice check or an approval threshold to release one stuck invoice removes that control from every property at once, and the change leaves no trace on the transaction that prompted it.
scr_ap_configuring_accounts_payable.ifSkipped: Setup is edited reactively to clear individual transactions, and controls quietly weaken across the whole portfolio.
gaap: SOX 404 ITGC — change management and logical access
COSO 2013 Principle 11 — general controls over technology
redFlags: Daily-task users holding Setup tab rights
Approval thresholds changed with no approval of the change itself
Configuration edited in production with no test and no record of the prior value
scr_ap_configuring_accounts_payable.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Setup > Payables configuration screens and Administration > Workflow setup, secured separately from transaction menus.

scr_ap_general_configuration.purpose: Covers the settings on the Configure Accounts Payable page — the general A/P behaviours such as defaults, required fields, duplicate checking and posting rules that apply before any vendor or payment-specific setup.
scr_ap_general_configuration.outcome: Portfolio-wide A/P defaults are set once and applied uniformly, so the same invoice behaves the same way whichever property it belongs to.
scr_ap_general_configuration.rootCause: Consistency is what makes a multi-entity portfolio reportable. When one property requires a purchase order reference and another does not, or duplicate detection is on in one region and off in another, the offshore team cannot apply a single SOP and the comparative analysis an owner asks for across their assets stops being like-for-like.
scr_ap_general_configuration.ifSkipped: A/P behaves differently per property, offshore SOPs cannot be standardized, and cross-property comparisons carry inconsistent data quality.
gaap: SOX 404 ITGC — configuration and change management
COSO 2013 Principle 12 — consistent deployment of policies
redFlags: Duplicate invoice checking disabled
Required coding fields turned off to speed entry
Default posting date set to the system date rather than the invoice date
scr_ap_general_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Setup > Payables system options controlling defaults, required fields and duplicate payable warnings.

scr_ap_configuring_the_ai_features_in_ac.purpose: Covers the AI capabilities available in A/P — AI invoice approvals, AI invoice intake scanning and AI contract scanning — which are enabled and tuned from the Company application's AI Configuration rather than inside A/P itself.
scr_ap_configuring_the_ai_features_in_ac.outcome: Automated capture and approval assistance is switched on with a defined scope, and the human review point in the workflow is explicitly retained.
scr_ap_configuring_the_ai_features_in_ac.rootCause: AI coding is genuinely useful on high-volume repeat spend like utilities and turn costs, where the same vendor bills the same account every month. It is least reliable on exactly the invoices that matter most — split-property allocations and capital versus repair calls — so the configuration has to keep a human review gate on those, or misclassified expense flows to the owner report and the tax return with no reviewer attached.
scr_ap_configuring_the_ai_features_in_ac.ifSkipped: Automated coding is accepted unreviewed, capital and repair decisions are made by a model, and no person can attest to the classification.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 11 — general controls over technology
SOX 404 — automated control reliance and review
Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — capital versus repair judgement
IRC §6001 — records supporting the position taken
redFlags: Auto-approval enabled above a material dollar threshold
AI-assigned GL coding accepted with no sample review
Multi-property allocations left to automated coding
Model confidence thresholds never revisited after go-live
scr_ap_configuring_the_ai_features_in_ac.yardi: Yardi Voyager: no one-to-one equivalent; the closest is PAYscan OCR capture with auto-coding assistance feeding the Payables workflow.

scr_ap_expense_report_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring the system for expense reports — enabling the feature, defining the expense categories available and setting the approval routing employee reimbursements must follow before they reach A/P.
scr_ap_expense_report_configuration.outcome: Expense reports route to an approver who is not the submitter, with categories that map to real property expense accounts.
scr_ap_expense_report_configuration.rootCause: The accountable-plan tax treatment depends on controls that have to be configured, not remembered: a receipt requirement at the $75 threshold, a submission deadline, and routing that never lets a person approve their own claim. Configure it loosely once and every reimbursement for the year inherits the weakness, with the correction landing on payroll as taxable wages.
scr_ap_expense_report_configuration.ifSkipped: Reimbursements are self-approved or unsubstantiated, and the whole plan fails the accountable-plan test, making payments taxable wages.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 10 — segregation in approval routing
redFlags: Routing that permits self-approval when the manager is absent
No receipt requirement configured at the $75 threshold
Expense categories not mapped to specific GL accounts
No submission deadline enforced
scr_ap_expense_report_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: no native expense-report configuration; approval routing for employee-vendor payables is set through Administration > Workflow setup.

scr_ap_full_service_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring the synchronization between the RealPage Financial Suite and OpsInvoice Processing so outsourced invoice capture flows into A/P — mapping properties, vendors and accounts across the two systems.
scr_ap_full_service_configuration.outcome: Captured invoices land in the right property and vendor record automatically, and mapping failures surface as exceptions rather than as silent misposts.
scr_ap_full_service_configuration.rootCause: The mapping between the processor's identifiers and the owner's property and vendor codes is the whole integration. A property added mid-quarter but never mapped means its invoices queue up invisibly at the processor while the site team assumes they are in the system, and the shortfall shows up as an unrecorded liability at the next close.
scr_ap_full_service_configuration.ifSkipped: Invoices for unmapped properties stall at the processor unnoticed, and month-end accruals miss an entire property's payables.
gaap: AICPA SSAE 18 and AU-C 402 — service organization control reliance
SOX 404 — interface and data transfer controls
redFlags: New properties onboarded without being added to the processor mapping
Sync error log never reviewed
Vendor codes diverging between the two systems after a vendor merge
No daily reconciliation of invoice counts sent versus received
scr_ap_full_service_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan integration setup mapping the scanning provider's data to Voyager properties, vendors and expense accounts.

scr_ap_a_p_account_labels.purpose: Covers adding and managing A/P account labels — the plain-language names shown to coders in place of raw account numbers, so a site manager picks the right expense account without memorizing the owner's chart.
scr_ap_a_p_account_labels.outcome: Coders select accounts by a label they recognize, and the underlying account number stays consistent with the owner's reporting template.
scr_ap_a_p_account_labels.rootCause: Coding accuracy at the property level depends almost entirely on how the account list reads to a non-accountant. A maintenance supervisor faced with a raw number list picks the first plausible line, which is how carpet replacement ends up in 6110 Repairs & Maintenance rather than 1530 Building Improvements — a labelling problem that surfaces as a capitalization error in the audit.
scr_ap_a_p_account_labels.ifSkipped: Site staff code by guesswork from unlabelled account numbers, and capital and repair spend blur together on the operating statement.
gaap: Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — coding drives the capitalization outcome
COSO 2013 — controls designed for the people who operate them
redFlags: Labels that mask a capital account behind a repairs-sounding name
Different labels for the same account across properties
Labels not updated when the owner changed their reporting template
scr_ap_a_p_account_labels.yardi: Yardi Voyager: account descriptions and Account Trees in Setup > Chart of Accounts control how accounts present to coders.

scr_ap_a_p_allocation_templates.purpose: Covers configuring A/P allocation templates by fixed amount or percentage — the reusable splits that distribute a single shared invoice across multiple properties or cost centres, such as a regional insurance premium or a portfolio-wide pest control contract.
scr_ap_a_p_allocation_templates.outcome: Shared costs split across properties on a stored, documented basis, applied identically each time the invoice recurs.
scr_ap_a_p_allocation_templates.rootCause: Cost allocation is the most frequently challenged item in an owner audit, because the owner is being charged for something they did not directly receive. A template makes the basis explicit and repeatable — units, square feet, headcount — so the allocation can be defended; an ad hoc split typed differently each month is exactly what a fee audit reclaims.
scr_ap_a_p_allocation_templates.ifSkipped: Shared costs are split by improvisation each month, the basis cannot be evidenced, and owners demand reimbursement of the allocation.
gaap: IRC §482 — arm's-length allocations between related parties
COSO 2013 — consistent application of a documented method
redFlags: Allocation percentages not summing to 100
Templates not updated after a property was acquired or sold
Allocation basis with no supporting unit or square-footage schedule
Costs allocated to properties the management agreement does not permit
scr_ap_a_p_allocation_templates.yardi: Yardi Voyager: expense pool allocation of shared payables across properties, or recurring journal entries using an allocation percent table.

scr_ap_management_fees_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring management fees — the fee basis, the percentage, the accounts included in the base and the properties each arrangement applies to, so the monthly fee calculation reproduces what the management agreement says.
scr_ap_management_fees_configuration.outcome: Each property carries a fee setup that mirrors its own management agreement, and the calculation can be traced back to specific revenue accounts.
scr_ap_management_fees_configuration.rootCause: No two management agreements define the fee base identically. One counts effective gross income including utility reimbursement, another excludes it, a third excludes other income entirely and a fourth has a floor. Configuring a single generic basis across a portfolio means most of the properties are being charged the wrong fee, in the manager's favour, every single month.
scr_ap_management_fees_configuration.ifSkipped: Fees are computed on a base the agreement does not support, producing a cumulative overcharge that becomes a refund claim on audit.
redFlags: One fee basis applied across properties with different agreements
4110 Utility Reimbursement included in a base the agreement excludes
Fee percentage not updated after an agreement amendment
Minimum fee floors not configured where the agreement sets one
scr_ap_management_fees_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Management Fees setup per property defining the income accounts forming the fee base and the fee percentage.

scr_ap_vendor_supplier_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring vendor records — the setup-side controls over what vendor data is required, which fields are mandatory before a vendor can be paid, and how vendors added from the All tab behave, as distinct from day-to-day vendor entry.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_configuration.outcome: Vendors cannot reach payable status without the compliance data the owner requires, because the system enforces it rather than a checklist.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_configuration.rootCause: Every W-9 that was never collected and every insurance certificate that was never requested traces back to a vendor setup that allowed the record to be created without them. Enforcing the requirement at configuration is the only version of this control that survives a busy week, because a procedural reminder loses to an urgent plumber at 5pm on a Friday.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_configuration.ifSkipped: Vendors are created without TIN or insurance and paid immediately, leaving 1099 gaps and uninsured contractors on site.
gaap: IRC §6109 and §3406 — TIN collection and backup withholding
redFlags: TIN not a required field before first payment
Vendor approval workflow disabled
Insurance expiry not blocking payment for trades that require coverage
Bank detail fields editable without a second approval
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor setup requirements and approval workflow in Setup > Payables, with VendorCafe enforcing compliance document collection.

scr_ap_tax_configuration.purpose: Covers tax configuration for A/P including VAT — tax authorities, tax details, tax schedules and schedule maps — plus the sales and use tax treatment that applies to taxable purchases and commercial rent in certain jurisdictions.
scr_ap_tax_configuration.outcome: Taxable A/P transactions carry the correct jurisdiction and rate, and tax amounts separate correctly from the expense they attach to.
scr_ap_tax_configuration.rootCause: Use tax is the exposure most US multifamily operators overlook on the payables side: when an out-of-state supplier ships appliances or materials without charging sales tax, the property still owes use tax to its own state. Unless the tax configuration captures it at invoice entry, the liability accrues silently until a state audit assesses it with interest and penalty.
scr_ap_tax_configuration.ifSkipped: Use tax on out-of-state purchases is never accrued, and the state assesses years of unpaid tax with interest and penalties.
gaap: State sales and use tax statutes
ASC 606-10-32-2A — net presentation of collected taxes
ASC 450-20 — accrual of probable tax assessments
ASC 740-10 — uncertain tax positions where material
reports: Sales and use tax accrual report
redFlags: Out-of-state material purchases with no use tax accrued
Tax rates not updated after a jurisdiction change
Tax amounts coded into the expense account rather than 2160 Sales Tax/VAT Payable
VAT configuration left enabled on US-only entities
scr_ap_tax_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: tax codes configured in Setup and applied on payables, with VAT and GST schedules for international entities.

scr_ap_loan_types.purpose: Covers configuring loan types — the classifications used where A/P handles debt-related disbursements such as mortgage principal and interest payments, escrow impounds and lender-required reserve fundings.
scr_ap_loan_types.outcome: Debt service payments split correctly between principal, interest and escrow instead of landing as a single expense charge.
scr_ap_loan_types.rootCause: A mortgage payment is three different accounting events in one cash movement: principal reduces 2210 Mortgage/Construction Loan Payable, interest hits 7010 Interest Expense, and the escrow portion is an asset in 1330 Tax & Insurance Escrow. Coded as one expense line, NOI is understated by the principal and escrow components and the debt balance on the balance sheet stops agreeing to the lender's statement.
scr_ap_loan_types.ifSkipped: Debt service posts as a single expense, NOI and the debt service coverage ratio reported to the lender are both wrong.
redFlags: Mortgage payments expensed in full rather than split
Escrow deposits expensed instead of recorded as 1330 Tax & Insurance Escrow
Loan balance not agreeing to the lender's amortization schedule
Construction period interest expensed rather than capitalized
scr_ap_loan_types.yardi: Yardi Voyager: loan and debt tracking with interest and principal payables, or Investment Manager's debt module for portfolio debt.

scr_ap_a_p_terms_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring A/P payment terms — the net day counts, discount terms such as 2/10 net 30, and due date calculation rules that determine when each vendor's invoices become payable.
scr_ap_a_p_terms_configuration.outcome: Invoice due dates calculate from the vendor's actual contracted terms, driving payment selection and the aging buckets on the A/P report.
scr_ap_a_p_terms_configuration.rootCause: Terms set the entire payment rhythm. Default every vendor to net 30 and the property either pays a net 15 contractor late enough to trigger a statutory prompt-payment claim on a construction job, or pays a net 60 supplier a month early and strips cash from a property that needed it for real estate taxes. Early payment discounts left unconfigured are pure forgone income.
scr_ap_a_p_terms_configuration.ifSkipped: Due dates are wrong across the board, aging buckets mislead the cash forecast, and available early-payment discounts go unclaimed.
gaap: State prompt-payment acts for construction contracts
ASC 405-10 — measurement of the liability net of available discounts
redFlags: Every vendor defaulted to net 30 regardless of contract
Discount terms configured but never selected in the payment run
Due dates calculating from entry date rather than invoice date
Construction vendors on terms longer than the state prompt-payment deadline
scr_ap_a_p_terms_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: payment terms defined in Setup and assigned on the vendor, driving due dates in Check Processing and the aged payables buckets.

scr_ap_asset_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring the system to track assets — the categories, useful lives and capitalization thresholds that determine which A/P purchases become fixed assets rather than period expense.
scr_ap_asset_configuration.outcome: The capitalization threshold and asset categories are enforced by configuration, so the capital-versus-expense line is drawn the same way on every property.
scr_ap_asset_configuration.rootCause: The de minimis safe harbor election has to be in place at the start of the tax year and applied consistently, and the system threshold is the practical evidence that it was. If one region capitalizes at $1,000 and another at $5,000 on the same owner's portfolio, neither the financial statement policy nor the tax election is defensible, and the IRS can reclassify either direction.
scr_ap_asset_configuration.ifSkipped: Capitalization is applied inconsistently across properties, and the de minimis safe harbor position cannot be supported on examination.
gaap: Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-1(f) — de minimis safe harbor election
Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — betterment, restoration and adaptation
redFlags: Threshold differing between properties of the same owner
Useful lives assigned per asset rather than by category
Threshold above $5,000 with no applicable financial statement to support it
Safe harbor election not made annually
scr_ap_asset_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager Fixed Assets: asset classes with default methods and lives in Setup, driving capitalization and depreciation.

scr_ap_contract_types.purpose: Covers creating and managing contract types — the classifications that separate service contracts, construction subcontracts and other vendor agreements so each follows the retainage, change order and lien waiver handling appropriate to it.
scr_ap_contract_types.outcome: Each contract behaves per its type, with construction agreements carrying retainage and waiver requirements that service agreements do not.
scr_ap_contract_types.rootCause: A recurring landscaping agreement and a roof replacement subcontract are both contracts and need entirely different treatment. Only one accrues retainage into 2015 Retainage Payable, only one exposes the owner to a mechanic's lien if a subcontractor goes unpaid, and only one has costs that belong in 1410 Construction in Progress. Type is what triggers the right handling automatically.
scr_ap_contract_types.ifSkipped: Construction agreements are processed like service contracts, retainage is not withheld, and lien exposure goes unmanaged.
gaap: State mechanic's lien and lien waiver statutes
redFlags: Construction subcontracts set up as service contract types
Retainage percentage not attached to the construction type
Contract types not requiring insurance certificates for on-site trades
No type distinguishing capital from operating agreements
scr_ap_contract_types.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Service Contracts for recurring agreements versus Job Cost > Contract for construction subcontracts with retainage and change orders.

scr_ap_automatic_payment_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring and scheduling automatic payments — the standing instructions that release payment for qualifying invoices on a defined cycle without a person initiating each run.
scr_ap_automatic_payment_configuration.outcome: Routine recurring payments release on schedule within defined limits, and the qualifying criteria are documented rather than implicit.
scr_ap_automatic_payment_configuration.rootCause: Automating the disbursement is automating the point where cash leaves the owner's account. The scheduling rules have to encode what a treasury analyst would otherwise check by hand — approval status, available cash in that property's 1110 Operating Cash, vendor active status — because a schedule that pays regardless of balance produces overdrafts on the properties with the tightest cash, which are always the ones already under owner scrutiny.
scr_ap_automatic_payment_configuration.ifSkipped: Scheduled runs pay unapproved or inactive-vendor invoices and overdraw properties whose cash position was never checked.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — recurring ACH origination
31 CFR Part 501 — OFAC screening on every payment
redFlags: Automatic runs with no available-cash test
Dollar ceilings never set on the schedule
Schedules that survived a vendor becoming inactive or disputed
Nobody named as the reviewer of each automatic run's output
scr_ap_automatic_payment_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Auto Pay in Check Processing with bank, property and date filters, plus scheduled EFT origination.

scr_ap_check_configuration.purpose: Covers configuring check preferences and signatures — check layout and MICR alignment, numbering, and the signature settings including the threshold at which a second signature becomes required.
scr_ap_check_configuration.outcome: Checks print correctly against the bank's specification, in an unbroken number sequence, with signature rules matching the owner's banking resolution.
scr_ap_check_configuration.rootCause: Check stock is a negotiable instrument and its configuration is a cash control, not a formatting preference. A misaligned MICR line gets the batch rejected at the bank after the payment date, a dual-signature threshold set above the typical capital invoice means the largest payments go out on a single signature, and a broken number sequence destroys the positive pay match for the whole run.
scr_ap_check_configuration.ifSkipped: Checks are rejected or clear on a single signature above the authorized limit, and positive pay cannot match the issued file.
gaap: UCC Article 3 — negotiable instruments and signature authority
UCC §4-406 — customer duty to examine statements
COSO 2013 — physical control over negotiable instruments
redFlags: Dual signature threshold set above the typical capital invoice amount
Signature image accessible to the person who prints the checks
Check number sequence gaps with no void record
MICR alignment unverified after a printer or stock change
scr_ap_check_configuration.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Setup > Bank check layout, MICR settings, next check number and signature thresholds.

scr_ap_electronic_payment_method_configu.purpose: Covers configuring electronic payment methods — the ACH and EFT origination settings, file formats and vendor enrolment requirements that let A/P pay without printing paper.
scr_ap_electronic_payment_method_configu.outcome: Electronic payments originate in the format the bank accepts, from vendors whose banking details were verified before enrolment.
scr_ap_electronic_payment_method_configu.rootCause: ACH is the fastest way to move money and the hardest to claw back — a business-to-business debit generally has no consumer-style return right once it settles. Vendor enrolment therefore has to carry an independent bank verification, a prenote where the bank supports it, and change controls, because the entire fraud scenario in property A/P is a convincing email asking to update remittance details.
scr_ap_electronic_payment_method_configu.ifSkipped: Funds are originated to unverified bank details with no realistic recovery path once the entry settles.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — origination, prenotification and authorization
COSO 2013 — verification of payee banking data
redFlags: Bank details entered from an emailed request without a call-back to a known number
No prenote before the first live ACH
The same person able to change vendor banking and release the ACH file
ACH file formats not retested after a bank migration
