scr_ap_third_party_payment_services_2.purpose: Covers configuring and using third-party payment services in RealPage Accounting — outsourced disbursement providers that print and mail checks or execute electronic payments on the owner's behalf from a funded account.
scr_ap_third_party_payment_services_2.outcome: Payments execute through the service provider with the funding, remittance and settlement legs each reconciled back to the property's cash account.
scr_ap_third_party_payment_services_2.rootCause: Outsourcing disbursement inserts a settlement account between the property and the vendor, and that account has to be reconciled like any other cash position. Funds sent to the provider but not yet disbursed are still the owner's money; treating the funding transfer as the payment overstates cash out, and unreconciled balances at the provider are a real cash exposure if the provider fails.
scr_ap_third_party_payment_services_2.ifSkipped: The provider's settlement balance is never reconciled, and cash in transit sits unaccounted between the property and its vendors.
gaap: AICPA SSAE 18 and AU-C 402 — service organization controls over disbursement
NACHA Operating Rules — third-party sender obligations
COSO 2013 — reconciliation of funds held by third parties
ASC 305 — cash and cash equivalents presentation
redFlags: Funding transfer recorded as the vendor payment
Provider settlement balance not reconciled monthly
Provider SOC 1 report not obtained
Failed or returned payments at the provider never reversed in A/P
scr_ap_third_party_payment_services_2.yardi: Yardi Voyager: outsourced check printing and payment services integrated with Payables check processing, reconciled through the bank rec.

scr_ap_common_tasks.purpose: Collects the cross-cutting procedures an accountant needs regardless of which A/P screen they are on — the shared mechanics of finding, filtering, attaching and exporting that recur throughout the application.
scr_ap_common_tasks.outcome: Common operations work the same way across A/P screens, so a technique learned on invoices transfers to vendors, payments and contracts.
scr_ap_common_tasks.rootCause: Training time on an offshore team is finite, and the cross-cutting mechanics are where it pays back most. An accountant who understands filtering and export once handles the owner's ad hoc question on any A/P object; one who learned each screen in isolation rebuilds the same query three times and produces three differently scoped answers.
scr_ap_common_tasks.ifSkipped: Each screen is learned in isolation, and the same owner question gets answered differently depending on where staff started.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 13 — quality of information used
redFlags: Inconsistent filter scoping producing different answers to the same owner question
Exports circulated without the filter criteria stated on them
scr_ap_common_tasks.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the common Find, filter and Excel export mechanics shared across Payables screens.

scr_ap_currency.purpose: Covers the multi-currency setup tasks in A/P — defining currencies and rates for owners or funds that transact outside a single reporting currency, which most US multifamily entities do not need.
scr_ap_currency.outcome: Foreign-currency payables are recorded at the transaction-date rate and remeasured at period end, with the gain or loss recognized.
scr_ap_currency.rootCause: Enabling multi-currency on an entity that only transacts in USD adds a rate field to every payable and a revaluation step to every close for no benefit — and worse, an unset or stale rate silently scales an invoice. For the cross-border funds that genuinely need it, the exposure runs the other way: unrevalued foreign payables misstate the liability at the reporting date.
scr_ap_currency.ifSkipped: Foreign payables are carried at a stale rate, and the liability and the FX gain or loss are both misstated at period end.
gaap: ASC 830-20 — foreign currency transaction gains and losses
COSO 2013 — documented and consistent rate source
redFlags: Multi-currency enabled on US-only entities
Rates not refreshed before period-end revaluation
Rate source undocumented or changed between periods
Realized and unrealized FX combined in a single account
scr_ap_currency.yardi: Yardi Voyager international: Setup > Currency and Exchange Rates with Financials > Currency Revaluation at period end.

scr_ap_attachments.purpose: Covers the tasks for working with attachments across the RealPage Financial Suite — adding, viewing and managing the documents that support A/P transactions, beyond the single-scan capture path.
scr_ap_attachments.outcome: Every material A/P transaction carries retrievable supporting documentation that travels with it into approval, review and audit sampling.
scr_ap_attachments.rootCause: Audit support fails on retrieval, not on existence. The invoice, the contract and the approval email usually exist somewhere — in a shared drive, in someone's mailbox, at the property office — but an auditor sampling 40 transactions needs them attached to the record, and the time cost of assembling them afterwards is measured in weeks of an offshore team's capacity.
scr_ap_attachments.ifSkipped: Support exists but cannot be produced on demand, and audit fieldwork stalls while the team reconstructs documentation.
redFlags: Attachments stored on a shared drive rather than on the record
Retention shorter than the seven years practice requires
Documents attached to the wrong transaction
Attachments containing vendor bank details accessible beyond the A/P role
scr_ap_attachments.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Document Management attachments accessible from the payable, vendor and contract records.

scr_ap_importing.purpose: Covers importing data into RealPage Accounting — how the import process works, what the file must contain, and the practices that make imports succeed rather than half-load, used for invoice batches, vendor loads and portfolio onboarding.
scr_ap_importing.outcome: Bulk data lands in A/P validated and reconciled to the source file, with rejected rows identified rather than silently dropped.
scr_ap_importing.rootCause: The failure mode on imports is the partial load. Eight hundred invoices submitted, seven hundred and forty accepted, and nobody reconciles the count — so sixty vendor invoices simply do not exist in the system, they never appear on the aging, and the shortfall becomes an unrecorded liability discovered at the audit. A control total agreed before and after is the only defence.
scr_ap_importing.ifSkipped: Imports load partially with no count reconciliation, and the missing records surface as unrecorded liabilities at close or audit.
gaap: SOX 404 — data conversion and interface controls
COSO 2013 Principle 13 — accuracy of information processing
redFlags: Record and dollar totals not agreed before and after the import
Error logs not reviewed and rejected rows never reprocessed
Imports run directly into production with no test load
Imported invoices bypassing the approval workflow
scr_ap_importing.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Administration > Import with ETL templates for vendor and payable loads, reconciled by control totals.

scr_ap_help_and_support_2.purpose: The support and documentation reference reached from the A/P configuration side — where a system administrator turns when a setup behaviour cannot be explained from the configuration screens alone.
scr_ap_help_and_support_2.outcome: Configuration questions are resolved against official documentation and support rather than by experimenting on live settings.
scr_ap_help_and_support_2.rootCause: Testing a configuration hypothesis in production is how a portfolio-wide control gets switched off. A setup question — why an approval is routing to the wrong person, why a payment method is not appearing — needs an answer from documentation or a support case, because the alternative is toggling settings on a live instance and discovering the side effect during next week's check run.
scr_ap_help_and_support_2.ifSkipped: Administrators test configuration theories on live settings, and side effects surface on production transactions a cycle later.
gaap: AICPA SSAE 18 — SOC 1 complementary user-entity controls
redFlags: Configuration experiments conducted in the production instance
Support case resolutions not written back into the configuration documentation
Repeat cases for the same setting, signalling an undocumented workaround
scr_ap_help_and_support_2.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Client Central documentation and support cases for configuration questions, with changes staged in a test database.

scr_ap_working_with_accounts_payable_rep.purpose: The reports book for A/P — how to customize and run the reports and charts covering what the company owes vendors and creditors, and how those outputs feed owner reporting and internal review.
scr_ap_working_with_accounts_payable_rep.outcome: A/P reporting is produced with deliberate filter, period and entity choices that match the question being answered.
scr_ap_working_with_accounts_payable_rep.rootCause: An A/P report is only as good as its scope, and scope errors are invisible on the printed page. A payables report run for one property when the owner asked about the fund, or run before the last invoice batch posted, reads perfectly and is wrong — and it becomes the cash-flow forecast an asset manager makes a funding decision on.
scr_ap_working_with_accounts_payable_rep.ifSkipped: Reports go out with unstated or wrong scope, and owners make funding decisions on payables figures that do not tie to the ledger.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 15 — communication with external parties
SEC Regulation G — non-GAAP measures where the owner is a public REIT
redFlags: Reports issued without the as-of date and entity scope stated on the face
Payables reports run before the period's final invoice batch posted
Charts presenting a filtered subset as if it were the portfolio
scr_ap_working_with_accounts_payable_rep.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Analytics > Payable Analytics and the Payables report set, with filters for book, period, property and bank.

scr_ap_a_p_reports.purpose: Describes each A/P report in detail in the same order as the menu, split between the A/P invoices group and the registers group, distinguishing standard prebuilt reports from those a user modifies with filters and formats.
scr_ap_a_p_reports.outcome: The accountant selects the report that actually answers the question rather than exporting a general list and rebuilding it in Excel.
scr_ap_a_p_reports.rootCause: The offshore reflex when asked an A/P question is to export the invoice list and pivot it, which produces an answer nobody else can reproduce. The standard reports already carry the right groupings and totals, and using them means the number in the owner package can be regenerated by a reviewer on demand — which is the difference between an answer and evidence.
scr_ap_a_p_reports.ifSkipped: Every A/P question is answered with a bespoke spreadsheet that no reviewer can reproduce or tie back to the ledger.
gaap: COSO 2013 Principle 13 — quality information for decision making
redFlags: Spreadsheet rebuilds used where a standard report exists
Modified report definitions saved over the standard version
Figures in the owner package that no standard report reproduces
scr_ap_a_p_reports.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the Payables report menu (Aged Payables, Payable Register, Check Register) with customizable filters and saved formats.

scr_ap_list_of_a_p_reports.purpose: The catalog of available A/P reports with what each one answers — days-to-pay performance and days past due by vendor, recurring invoice status and frequency, A/P Invoice Analysis of expense line items, the asset listing and the Check Register.
scr_ap_list_of_a_p_reports.outcome: The accountant can go from a question to the right report name without opening several to find out what they contain.
scr_ap_list_of_a_p_reports.rootCause: Days-to-pay is the report property accountants most often do not know exists and most need. It answers the question an asset manager actually asks — are we paying our vendors on terms, or is the property quietly financing itself on the landscaper's patience — and it is the early signal of a cash problem long before the aging looks alarming.
scr_ap_list_of_a_p_reports.ifSkipped: Useful diagnostic reports go unused, and payment performance deterioration is only noticed when a vendor stops servicing the property.
gaap: ASC 450-20 — disclosure where late payment creates a contingency
redFlags: Days-to-pay lengthening across consecutive months on the same property
Recurring invoice status showing schedules that stopped generating
Vendors on the aging with balances older than their contract term
scr_ap_list_of_a_p_reports.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Analytics > Payable Analytics for aging and payment performance, with the Payable Register and Check Register reports.

scr_ap_reports_workflow.purpose: Describes the report lifecycle — run it, inspect the result, click Customize to change parameters and rerun if it is wrong, then process and store the output, and memorize the settings if it will be needed again.
scr_ap_reports_workflow.outcome: A report that answers the question is stored as evidence and its parameters saved, so the next cycle reproduces it identically.
scr_ap_reports_workflow.rootCause: Owner packages have to be reproducible month over month, and that only holds if the report parameters are memorized rather than retyped. A package built from hand-set filters drifts — one month includes a property that closed, the next excludes a book — and the resulting trend line an asset manager reads is comparing two different populations.
scr_ap_reports_workflow.ifSkipped: Report parameters are retyped each month, scope drifts between cycles, and period-over-period comparisons in the owner package are unreliable.
gaap: ASC 205 and ASC 220 — comparative presentation consistency
SOX 404 — evidence retention for reported figures
redFlags: Owner package reports rebuilt by hand each month
Stored outputs not retained as evidence of what was issued
Memorized settings not updated after a property acquisition or disposition
scr_ap_reports_workflow.yardi: Yardi Voyager: report filters saved as user-defined report settings and scheduled through the Report Scheduler for repeatable packages.

scr_ap_vendors_reports.purpose: The vendor-side report group — Vendor Aging, Vendor List, Vendor Insurance, the 1099 and 1096 forms and reports, the 1099 file creation and the electronic filing output.
scr_ap_vendors_reports.outcome: Vendor balances, compliance status and year-end information returns can all be produced from a single report family.
scr_ap_vendors_reports.rootCause: These reports carry two separate deadlines the property accountant owns. Vendor Insurance drives whether an uninsured trade is working on the asset today, which is a live liability exposure; the 1099 set drives the January filing where a missing or mismatched TIN turns into a per-return penalty multiplied across every contractor the portfolio paid.
scr_ap_vendors_reports.ifSkipped: Uninsured vendors keep working on site and 1099 filings go out incomplete, drawing IRS penalties and backup withholding exposure.
gaap: IRC §6721 and §6722 — penalties for incorrect returns
redFlags: Vendors paid over the reporting threshold with no TIN on file
Insurance report showing expired coverage for active on-site trades
Attorneys not flagged as reportable despite incorporation
1099 file created but never transmitted
scr_ap_vendors_reports.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > 1099 Processing with the 1099 report and export, plus vendor aging and insurance tracking reports.

scr_ap_a_p_invoices_and_registers.purpose: The invoice and register report group — A/P Invoice Register, Check Register, RealPage Payments, A/P Invoice Analysis, Recurring A/P Invoice Status, Selected A/P Invoices, Reclassification and Management Fee reports.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_and_registers.outcome: Every posted A/P transaction can be traced through a register, and every reclass and fee calculation has a report supporting it.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_and_registers.rootCause: This group is what an auditor works from. The Invoice Register proves the population of liabilities recorded, the Check Register proves what was disbursed against them, and the Reclassification report exposes how much coding was corrected after the fact — which is itself a measure of whether the coding control at the front of the process is working.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_and_registers.ifSkipped: There is no register-level trail from recorded liability to disbursement, and audit testing falls back on sampling individual screens.
gaap: SOX 404 — audit trail from liability to disbursement
ASC 850-10 — management fee as a related-party charge
redFlags: Reclassification volume rising each month
Check Register total not agreeing to cash disbursed on the bank rec
Selected invoices report not reviewed before the payment run releases
Register totals not tied to the 2010 Accounts Payable movement for the period
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_and_registers.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payable Register and Check Register reports, with the management fee report from Financials > Management Fees.

scr_ap_working_with_reports.purpose: Covers the general mechanics of running reports — parameters, formats, output destinations and distribution — separate from financial statement creation, which is documented on its own.
scr_ap_working_with_reports.outcome: Reports are produced in the right format for their destination and distributed only to recipients entitled to see that scope of data.
scr_ap_working_with_reports.rootCause: A/P output carries vendor banking details, TINs and, on final account statements, resident information. Exporting it moves that data outside the application's access controls and outside the SOC 1 boundary, so an aging emailed to a broad distribution list is both a data exposure and a version-control problem the moment the next invoice batch posts.
scr_ap_working_with_reports.ifSkipped: Exports carrying vendor TINs and banking data circulate beyond their entitled audience, outside every access control the system applies.
gaap: SOC 1 — data leaving the service organization boundary
COSO 2013 Principle 15 — communication with external parties
IRC §6103 concepts around taxpayer identifying information handling
redFlags: Exports containing vendor TINs or bank details sent by unencrypted email
Reports distributed without the as-of date on the face
Stale exports circulating after a subsequent invoice batch posted
Distribution lists never reviewed against current recipients
scr_ap_working_with_reports.yardi: Yardi Voyager: report output to PDF or Excel with distribution through the Report Scheduler, subject to user and property security.
